question: Change the ScrapeInterval field in GlobalConfig from model.Duration to a new typed Duration with validation constraints. GlobalConfig is embedded by Thanos, Mimir, and Grafana for configuring Prometheus-compatible scrape and evaluation intervals. Any code that assigns model.Duration values to ScrapeInterval will break.

files_to_modify.why: Contains the GlobalConfig struct definition where ScrapeInterval is declared as model.Duration (line 468). Also contains DefaultGlobalConfig initialization assigning model.Duration(1 * time.Minute) to ScrapeInterval (line 167), the ScrapeConfig struct with its own ScrapeInterval field of model.Duration (line 759), UnmarshalYAML validation logic comparing ScrapeInterval == 0 and assigning defaults (lines 648-655, 890-897), and isZero() checking ScrapeInterval == 0 (line 692). All model.Duration assignments, comparisons with 0, and type casts must change to the new typed Duration.

Contains 63 occurrences of ScrapeInterval assignments using model.Duration() in test structs. Every test that constructs GlobalConfig or ScrapeConfig with ScrapeInterval: model.Duration(...) will break. Includes expectedConf (line 91), ScrapeConfigOptions struct (line 2783), and dozens of test case struct literals throughout the file (lines 91, 219, 345, 456, 519, 559, 605, 651, 687, 731, 772, 820, 858, 899, 933, 970, 1007, 1044, 1078, 1120, 1161, 1199, 1236, 1277, 1321, 1385, 1419, 1464, 1515, 1556, 1598, 1635, 1674, 2723, 2842-2997, etc.).

Contains 4 references to ScrapeInterval: time.Duration(sp.config.ScrapeInterval) casts at lines 308, 331, 456 for computing reload intervals and target scrape intervals, and zeroConfig() setting ScrapeInterval = 0 at line 2222. The time.Duration() casts from model.Duration will break with the new typed Duration.

Contains 45 occurrences of ScrapeInterval assignments using model.Duration() in test ScrapeConfig struct literals. Every test constructing config.ScrapeConfig{ScrapeInterval: model.Duration(...)} breaks. Key locations include lines 369, 415, 551, 631, 714, 940, 1012, 4230, 4235, 4280, 4307, 4318, 4330, 4343, 4359, 4373, 4384, 4396, 4408, 4421, 4498, 4522, 4613, 4674, 4819, 4892, 5503, 5654, 6082, 6102, 6127, 6221, 6577, 6650, 6755.

Line 295 parses ScrapeIntervalLabel from target labels. Line 572 calls cfg.ScrapeInterval.String() to produce the scrape interval label value. Line 612 parses the interval label string. The .String() call relies on model.Duration's String() method; the new type must provide compatible formatting.

Line 1070 defines ScrapeInterval as a string field in the target API response struct. Line 1222 reads ScrapeInterval from target labels via target.GetValue(model.ScrapeIntervalLabel). While this uses string values, changes to how ScrapeInterval is formatted may affect API output.

Lines 140 and 146 contain verifyScrapeInterval() test helper that validates scrape interval via the /api/v1/status/config endpoint after reload. Tests verify the string representation of the scrape interval in YAML config output.

Line 488 constructs config.GlobalConfig{} struct literal with ExternalLabels when configuring remote write storage. While it doesn't set ScrapeInterval directly, it uses the GlobalConfig struct type which now has a changed field type. If the new Duration type has different zero-value semantics or requires explicit initialization, this code may need updating.

Line 344 uses reflect.TypeOf(config.GlobalConfig{}) for type switching, and line 498 defines validateGlobalConfig(cfg config.GlobalConfig) which accepts the GlobalConfig by value. While these don't directly reference ScrapeInterval, they operate on the GlobalConfig struct. If the new Duration type affects reflection behavior, serialization, or requires new validation, this code must be updated.

Lines 1122-1131 construct config.GlobalConfig{} struct literals for testing validation (setting SMTPAuthPasswordFile). Lines 1203 and 1214 construct config.GlobalConfig{} with HTTPConfig for nested validation tests. These struct literals use the GlobalConfig type and would be affected if the new Duration type changes initialization semantics.

Vendored copy of Prometheus config/config.go with identical 13 ScrapeInterval references. Contains the same GlobalConfig struct definition (line 468), DefaultGlobalConfig (line 167), validation logic (lines 648-655, 890-897), and isZero (line 692). All model.Duration assignments and comparisons must be updated when re-vendoring.

type_change.new_type: Duration (new typed Duration with validation constraints)
type_change.description: Changes the ScrapeInterval field in GlobalConfig (and ScrapeInterval in ScrapeConfig) from model.Duration to a new typed Duration that includes validation constraints. This is a breaking change because model.Duration is used pervasively in struct literal initialization (e.g., ScrapeInterval: model.Duration(1 * time.Minute)), zero-value comparisons (ScrapeInterval == 0), and time.Duration casts (time.Duration(sp.config.ScrapeInterval)). All downstream consumers that construct GlobalConfig or ScrapeConfig with model.Duration values, compare against numeric zero, or cast to time.Duration must be updated.

breaking_patterns: ScrapeInterval: model.Duration(...) - struct literal initialization with model.Duration values
time.Duration(config.ScrapeInterval) - explicit cast from model.Duration to time.Duration
ScrapeInterval == 0 - zero-value comparison assuming model.Duration is int64
ScrapeInterval > ScrapeTimeout - direct comparison between model.Duration fields
DefaultGlobalConfig.ScrapeInterval - accessing default config fields of the old type
